note: IF YOUR CHANGE MOVES A CENSUS VALUE, gate-commit WILL NOT TELL YOU. Measured during The Confidant: grep -c census_sentinel docs/timings/subfloor-roster.tsv returns 0. The file windows/lab/tests/suite/census_sentinel.rs is COMPILED by gate-commit and never RUN by it, because the roster selects by exact test name and that binary has no entry. So a branch whose census values have moved goes green locally, every commit, and the first thing that notices is a full stage gate or a merge — minutes into a chamber run rather than seconds into a local one. HOW IT BIT: this campaign added six concepts and granted cultures words for them, which legitimately moves exposure-sound-kobold, homophony-count-kobold and homophony-count-bugbear. gate-commit stayed green through all of it. I reported that green as evidence the branch was healthy and it was not evidence of that at all. THE CHECK THAT ACTUALLY ANSWERS IT, and it is seconds: cargo test -p hornvale-lab --test suite -- census_sentinel. Run it after anything that touches domains/, worldgen, or a lexicon. Its failure message is genuinely good — it names the moved columns with live-versus-committed values and tells you the two remedies (refresh the goldens on lefford, or waive a host-divergent metric WITH A REASON in sentinel-waivers.txt). SECOND TRAP IN THE SAME EPISODE, and it is the more general one: PRE-EXISTING IS A CLAIM ABOUT main. A subagent reported two failures as pre-existing having verified them on a clean checkout of HEAD — but HEAD was the campaign branch, so all that established was that the failures did not depend on its uncommitted work. Running the same test on origin/main in a scratch worktree showed it PASSES there. Ours, not inherited. Three separate people made a version of that error in one night here: a symmetric git diff read as directional, pre-existing measured against the wrong baseline, and a green gate read as broader coverage than it has. Same shape every time — a real command, correctly run, answering a narrower question than the claim attached to it.
